subject: physics
question_text: Define Young’s modulus, Bulk modulus and Shear modulus.

verification.note: Asked in TS March 2023 (Q17) — TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, Section B, 4 marks. The four-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: Y = longitudinal stress / longitudinal strain = FL/Ae; K = −volume stress / volume strain = −PV/ΔV, the minus sign written because ΔV is negative when P rises, which keeps K positive; η = shearing stress / shearing strain = (F/A)/θ. All three carry the SI unit N m⁻².

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Modulus of elasticity
lines: Inside the elastic limit, stress is
proportional to strain. The ratio of stress
to strain is a constant for the material and
is called its modulus of elasticity.
Strain has no unit, so every modulus carries
the unit of stress, N m⁻².
steps.margin_note: First mark. One sentence of Hooke's law plus the ratio, and the unit N m⁻² for all three.
steps.why: The three moduli in this question are the same ratio applied to the three types of stress, so writing the general form once makes each definition below one line long.
common_mistakes: Writing strain / stress. The modulus is stress divided by strain.
Giving a modulus no unit because strain has none. Strain has no unit, so the modulus keeps the unit of stress.

recall.must_convey: That inside the elastic limit stress is proportional to strain and their ratio is the modulus of elasticity, with unit newton per metre squared.
accept: stress by strain is a constant

steps.memory_tip: Every modulus is stress ÷ strain. Strain has no unit, so every modulus is in N m⁻².

steps.label: Young’s modulus
lines: 1. Young’s modulus Y is the ratio of
longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain.
SI unit: N m⁻². It measures the change in
length of a wire under a stretching force.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The words longitudinal stress and longitudinal strain earn it; the formula supports them.
steps.why: Y is the modulus for a stress that acts along one direction, which is why only the length changes and the strain is e/L.
common_mistakes: Writing Y = F/Ae and losing the L. The original length L is in the numerator.
Using Young’s modulus for a body under fluid pressure. That case needs the bulk modulus.

recall.must_convey: That Young’s modulus is longitudinal stress divided by longitudinal strain, equal to F L by A e.

steps.memory_tip: Y is the length modulus: a stretched wire changes its length, so strain is e/L.

steps.label: Bulk modulus
lines: 2. Bulk modulus K is the ratio of volume
stress to volume strain.
The minus sign is written because a rise in
pressure decreases the volume, so ΔV is
negative. The sign keeps K positive.
SI unit: N m⁻².
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Write the minus sign and say in one line why it is there.
steps.why: Without the minus sign K would come out negative for every real material, because an increase in pressure always decreases the volume.
common_mistakes: Omitting the minus sign. Some guides leave it out, but it is what keeps K positive.
Reading ΔV as the volume. ΔV is the CHANGE in volume and V is the original volume.

recall.must_convey: That the bulk modulus is minus volume stress divided by volume strain, minus P V by delta V, and the minus sign keeps K positive.
accept: minus P V by delta V
the minus sign keeps K positive
heard_as: minus P V by delta V

steps.memory_tip: Pressure up, volume down, so ΔV is negative. The minus sign turns K positive again.

steps.label: Shear modulus
lines: 3. Shear modulus η, also called the modulus
of rigidity, is the ratio of shearing stress
to shearing strain θ.
SI unit: N m⁻². It measures the change in
shape of a body under a tangential force.

lines.text: Each modulus = its stress ÷ its strain

steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The second name, modulus of rigidity, is worth writing — some papers use it.
steps.why: Shearing strain is measured as the angle θ through which a face is turned, so it is already a pure number and needs no division by a length.
common_mistakes: Writing the shearing strain as a length divided by a length. It is the angle θ in radians.
Using the symbol G without saying it is the same as η. Both symbols are accepted.

recall.must_convey: That the shear modulus, or modulus of rigidity, is shearing stress divided by shearing strain theta, with unit newton per metre squared.
accept: F by A divided by theta
reject: minus P V by delta V

steps.memory_tip: Shearing strain is the angle θ, so η = (F/A)/θ needs no length at all.

insider_note: One mark for each modulus. The minus sign in K is part of its mark, and every definition needs its unit N m⁻².
